content.text:
Here’s a **first-time, seven-day China itinerary** that balances big sights, food, history, and efficient travel: **Beijing → Xi’an → Shanghai**. It’s fast-paced but very doable by high-speed rail and gives you China’s imperial, ancient, and modern sides.

## Overview

| Day | City | Main focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Beijing | Arrival, hutongs, local food |
| 2 | Beijing | Forbidden City, Tiananmen area, Temple of Heaven |
| 3 | Beijing | Great Wall day trip |
| 4 | Xi’an | High-speed train, Muslim Quarter, city walls |
| 5 | Xi’an | Terracotta Warriors, Big Wild Goose Pagoda |
| 6 | Shanghai | High-speed train or flight, Bund, Yu Garden |
| 7 | Shanghai | French Concession, museums, departure |

---

## Day 1 — Arrive in Beijing

**Base:** Beijing, ideally near Dongcheng, Wangfujing, Qianmen, or a subway line.

After arrival, keep it light.

**Do:**
- Walk around **Wangfujing** or **Qianmen Street**
- Explore a **hutong** area such as Nanluoguxiang or Shichahai
- Eat your first proper Beijing meal

**Food ideas:**
- Peking duck
- Zhajiangmian — Beijing-style noodles
- Dumplings
- Lamb skewers

**Tip:** Set up **Alipay** or **WeChat Pay** before or immediately after arrival. China is very mobile-payment heavy.

---

## Day 2 — Imperial Beijing

Start early.

**Morning: Forbidden City / Palace Museum**  
Book in advance if possible. The Forbidden City is usually closed on Mondays except some public holidays, so avoid scheduling it for a Monday. Advance booking is strongly recommended, especially in peak seasons. ([chinadiscovery.com](https://www.chinadiscovery.com/beijing/forbidden-city/how-to-book-tickets.html?utm_source=openai))

**Route:**
- Tiananmen Square area
- Forbidden City
- Jingshan Park for the classic view over the palace rooftops

**Afternoon: Temple of Heaven**
- One of Beijing’s most beautiful imperial sites
- Great for photography and people-watching

**Evening:**
- Dinner in Sanlitun, Dongsi, or Qianmen
- Optional: acrobatics show or Peking opera sampler

---

## Day 3 — Great Wall Day Trip

Best choice for a first visit: **Mutianyu Great Wall**.

Why Mutianyu:
- Scenic
- Restored but not as intense as some sections
- Easier logistics than wilder sections
- Cable car/chairlift options

**Plan:**
- Leave Beijing around 7:00–8:00 am
- Spend 2–3 hours on the Wall
- Return mid-afternoon

**Evening:**
- Relax in Beijing
- Try hotpot or a craft beer area around Beixinqiao / Dongzhimen

**Alternative:** If you want a more rugged, less touristy Wall experience, choose **Jinshanling**, but it takes longer and is more strenuous.

---

## Day 4 — Beijing to Xi’an

Take a **high-speed train from Beijing West to Xi’an North**. The ride is usually around 4.5–6 hours depending on the train.

Foreign visitors can book China high-speed rail using a passport through the official **12306** platform or through travel booking apps; bring the same passport used for booking when you travel. ([tocntravel.com](https://www.tocntravel.com/insights/china-high-speed-train-tickets/?utm_source=openai))

**Afternoon in Xi’an:**
- Check into hotel
- Walk or bike the **Xi’an City Wall**
- Visit the **Bell Tower** and **Drum Tower**

**Evening: Muslim Quarter**
- Try roujiamo — Chinese-style meat sandwich
- Biangbiang noodles
- Lamb skewers
- Persimmon cakes
- Pomegranate juice

**Base:** Stay inside or just outside the old city wall for convenience.

---

## Day 5 — Terracotta Warriors and Ancient Xi’an

**Morning: Terracotta Army**
- Go early
- Hire a guide or use an audio guide; it makes the site much more meaningful
- Expect a half-day visit including transport

**Afternoon:**
- Big Wild Goose Pagoda
- Great Tang All Day Mall / Datang Everbright City area
- Shaanxi History Museum if you love history and can secure tickets

**Evening:**
- Tang-style performance dinner, or
- Casual food crawl around the old city

---

## Day 6 — Xi’an to Shanghai

You have two good options:

### Option A: Fly Xi’an → Shanghai
Best if you want to save time.

### Option B: High-speed train Xi’an North → Shanghai Hongqiao
More scenic and comfortable, but longer — often around 6–7+ hours.

**Afternoon/evening in Shanghai:**
- Walk the **Bund**
- Cross to **Lujiazui** for skyline views
- Optional: Shanghai Tower observation deck
- Dinner in Xintiandi, the Bund area, or Huangpu

**Base:** Stay near People’s Square, Nanjing Road, Jing’an, Xintiandi, or the Former French Concession.

---

## Day 7 — Shanghai Highlights and Departure

**Morning:**
- **Yu Garden** and the old-city bazaar
- Walk to the Bund if you didn’t do it the night before

**Afternoon:**
Choose one:
- **Former French Concession** for leafy streets, cafés, boutiques
- **Shanghai Museum** for culture and history
- **Tianzifang** for lanes and shops
- **M50** art district if you like contemporary art

**Evening:**
- Depart from Shanghai, or add an extra night if your flight is the next morning.

---

## Recommended Route

For most travelers:

**Fly into Beijing → train to Xi’an → fly or train to Shanghai → fly out of Shanghai**

This avoids backtracking and gives a satisfying north-to-south arc.

---

## Where to Stay

**Beijing:**  
- Dongcheng  
- Wangfujing  
- Qianmen  
- Near a subway station inside the 2nd Ring Road

**Xi’an:**  
- Inside the city wall  
- Near Bell Tower / South Gate  
- Near a metro station

**Shanghai:**  
- People’s Square  
- Jing’an  
- Xintiandi  
- Former French Concession  
- Nanjing Road / Bund area

---

## Practical Notes

- **Visa / entry:** If you’re a U.S. passport holder or from another eligible country and are transiting onward to a third country or region, China’s 240-hour visa-free transit policy may apply. It allows eligible travelers to enter through designated ports and stay within permitted areas for up to 240 hours, but you need a confirmed onward ticket to a third country or region. Always verify your exact route before booking. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/english.www.gov.cn/news/202412/17/content_WS6760ead6c6d0868f4e8ee0c1.html?utm_source=openai))  
- **Apps to install:** Alipay, WeChat, Baidu Maps or Apple Maps, Trip.com, 12306, Pleco, translation app.
- **Payment:** Cash is less commonly used than mobile payment, though major hotels still accept cards.
- **Trains:** Book high-speed rail in advance, especially around Chinese holidays.
- **Avoid if possible:** Chinese New Year, May Day holiday, and National Day week, when domestic travel is extremely busy.

---

## Best Time to Go

Best overall months:
- **April–May**
- **September–October**

Hotter and more humid:
- July–August

Colder but less crowded:
- December–February, except Chinese New Year travel period

---

## If You Prefer a Slower Trip

If you don’t want to change cities twice, do:

**Beijing 4 days + Shanghai 3 days**

You’d skip Xi’an, but the trip would be easier and more relaxed.

My top recommendation for a first seven-day China trip, though, is still:

**Beijing 3 nights → Xi’an 2 nights → Shanghai 2 nights.**
